---
title: Testing your API client
---

You have written an `ApiClient` subclass for a REST API hosted in Azure
behind Entra ID. Its tests should run in CI on every pull request, and CI
has no Azure: no `az login`, no service principal you would want to put in
a runner, and an API you do not want a test to change. dazure's own CI
works the same way ([design decision D23](https://github.com/pedrobtz/py-dazure/blob/main/.agents/design.md#10-decisions):
Azure is tested by hand, CI only with simple mocks): what needs real Azure is checked
by hand, and the automated tests touch neither Azure nor the network.

So the tests replace the two things the client talks to:

- **the API**, with [respx](https://lundberg.github.io/respx/), which
  answers `httpx` requests from routes you declare. `ApiClient` is an
  `httpx` client, so respx mocks it with no change to the client;
- **the credential**, with `dazure.testing.StaticTokenCredential`, a
  `TokenCredential` that hands out a fixed token and records the scopes it
  was asked for. Pass it as `credential=`, which wins over
  `app_credential()`.

Everything else is the real client: its URL templating, request bodies,
parsing, validation, errors and retries.

## The example: the Petstore as an Azure-hosted API

The public Swagger Petstore needs no token, so the example in
`examples/azure_petstore.py` pretends it does. It is the Petstore client of
the [REST client](rest-client.qmd) page with an Entra ID scope and its own
service-principal variables:

<!-- snippet: class AzurePetStoreClient(PetStoreClient): -->
{{< include examples/azure_petstore.py lines="24-32" >}}

Its tests are in `examples/tests/` and run in dazure's CI. They need
`pytest`, `respx` and `pytest-socket` in your dev dependencies:

```sh
uv add --dev pytest respx pytest-socket
```

## The fixtures: `conftest.py`

Copy this file next to your tests and change the client, the URL and the
names:

<!-- snippet: @pytest.fixture -->
{{< include examples/tests/conftest.py lines="30-53" >}}

`api` is a respx router for the API's base URL, so routes are written as
paths (`api.get("/pet/7")`). `assert_all_called=False` lets a test declare
routes it does not end up calling. `credential` is a fresh
`StaticTokenCredential` per test, so `credential.calls` holds only that
test's calls. `store` is the client under test, built on both.

## The tests

Each test scripts the API's answer, calls a method, and checks what came
back and what was sent. A successful call returns a validated model, and
the request carried the fake token, asked for with the class's scope:

<!-- snippet: def test_get_pet_returns_a_validated_pet_and_sends_the_token( -->
{{< include examples/tests/test_azure_petstore.py lines="27-39" >}}

The scope is written out rather than read from the class, so a test fails
if the class's scope changes by mistake.

A request body is checked as it was sent, from the recorded request: the
model's camelCase aliases, and only the fields that were set.

<!-- snippet: def test_add_pet_sends_the_model_as_json(api: respx.MockRouter, store: AzurePetStoreClient) -> None: -->
{{< include examples/tests/test_azure_petstore.py lines="42-49" >}}

Failures are scripted the same way. A body that does not validate is a
`ResponseParseError`; a 404 is the client's own domain error, chained to
the `ApiError`:

<!-- snippet: def test_a_malformed_pet_is_a_parse_error( -->
{{< include examples/tests/test_azure_petstore.py lines="52-68" >}}

`side_effect` with a list answers each call in turn, which scripts a
retry. `ApiClient` retries 429, 503 and connection failures, waiting
between attempts with `time.sleep`; its `sleep=` argument takes the
function to wait with instead, so `sleep=waits.append` makes the test
instant and records the waits:

<!-- snippet: def test_503_is_retried(api: respx.MockRouter, credential: StaticTokenCredential) -> None: -->
{{< include examples/tests/test_azure_petstore.py lines="71-93" >}}

## Which credential the client picks

Whether a deployment gets its service principal and a developer their
`az login` depends on the environment, and can be tested without signing
in: `app_credential()` only builds the azure-identity credential, it
fetches no token until a request is made. Set or clear the variables with
`monkeypatch`, build the client, and check `client.credential`, the
credential it chose, by type:

<!-- snippet: def test_service_principal_when_its_variables_are_set(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None: -->
{{< include examples/tests/test_azure_petstore.py lines="99-117" >}}

Clear `AZURE_TOKEN_CREDENTIALS` too: a value on the runner would choose the
mode instead. These tests run with the network blocked (below), so building
`ClientSecretCredential` and the `az login` chain is checked to make no
connection.

## Offline by construction

Two guards make sure no test reaches the network, even by mistake.

- **respx, for `httpx`.** While the `api` router is active, a request no
  route matches raises an `AssertionError` ("not mocked") instead of going
  out: respx's `assert_all_mocked=True`, its default, which the fixture
  keeps.
- **pytest-socket, for everything else.** An autouse fixture blocks every
  socket for each test in the directory: MSAL and azure-identity fetching a
  token, another HTTP client, even a DNS lookup fail with
  `SocketBlockedError`. Unix sockets stay allowed, for local tooling.

<!-- snippet: @pytest.fixture(autouse=True) -->
{{< include examples/tests/conftest.py lines="22-27" >}}

Being a fixture in `conftest.py`, it covers only the tests in that
directory; tests elsewhere that need a local server keep their sockets.
(`pytest --disable-socket` does the same for a whole run.) Both guards are
themselves tested:

<!-- snippet: def test_an_unmocked_request_fails(api: respx.MockRouter, store: AzurePetStoreClient) -> None: -->
{{< include examples/tests/test_azure_petstore.py lines="123-133" >}}

pytest-socket also issues a warning when it blocks a socket, which
`pytest.warns` expects here; under `filterwarnings = ["error"]` an
unexpected block fails the test either way.

## Without respx: `httpx.MockTransport`

If you would rather not add a dependency, `httpx.MockTransport` takes a
function from request to response. Pass it as the client's `transport=`:

```python
import httpx
import pytest

from dazure.testing import StaticTokenCredential


@pytest.fixture
def store():
    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        if request.method == "GET" and request.url.path == "/api/v3/pet/7":
            return httpx.Response(200, json=PET)
        return httpx.Response(404)

    transport = httpx.MockTransport(handler)
    with AzurePetStoreClient(credential=StaticTokenCredential(), transport=transport) as client:
        yield client
```

respx adds the routing, the call recording and the unmocked-request check,
and needs no change to how the client is built.

## What stays manual

The fakes stand in for Entra ID and the API, so these tests cannot tell
you that the real ones agree. Keep a short live check, run by hand or on a
schedule with real credentials, outside the CI suite:

- the scope and the app registration: a real token for `scope` is accepted
  by the API;
- the service principal, managed identity or workload identity of each
  deployment signs in;
- the real API still answers in the shape the models expect.

dazure does the same with an opt-in live test of the Petstore example
(`DAZURE_LIVE_HTTP=1`) and a manual checklist for everything that needs
Azure.
